headline: Rooftop solar project brings stable collective income to SW China village
article:
KUNMING, China (Xinhua) -- Gangba village in southwest China's Yunnan Province is transitioning from a traditional, weather-dependent agricultural economy to a stable clean energy model through rooftop distributed photovoltaic (PV) projects.

In this village, the economic foundation previously relied mainly on sheep raising. However, this traditional livelihood was subject to market fluctuations and environmental factors, resulting in unstable incomes. To break this cycle and promote rural revitalization, the village has introduced a 50-kilowatt rooftop distributed PV project.

The project is scheduled to be connected to the power grid by the end of 2025. Once operational, the solar panels installed on village rooftops are expected to generate about 74,000 kilowatt-hours of clean electricity annually.

"Previously, our income was mainly from sheep raising, which was quite unstable," the village Party secretary said. "The rooftop PV project will bring over 24,000 yuan in stable collective income per year."

This mechanism transforms idle rooftop space into a productive asset. By harnessing solar power, the village not only reduces its reliance on vulnerable farming methods but also creates a predictable revenue stream for the collective economy.

The initiative exemplifies a win-win approach to green development. It integrates clean energy generation with rural revitalization, ensuring that ecological and economic goals advance together. Ultimately, the project secures a sustainable livelihood for the villagers while contributing to the broader transition toward low-carbon energy.
